Documentation → Safeguards → Overview → Writing to appliances

Safeguards — writing to appliances

The gates in front of every change SATOM sends to an appliance — read-only command validation, dry run before apply, lease locks and change-request gating checked again at run time.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereAppliance pages, the object editors, the device and SSH consoles, firmware upgrade and scheduled actions
On this page
  • Why this area has the most gates
  • The guards
  • Where to read more

Why this area has the most gates#

Writing to an appliance is the part of SATOM that can take a customer offline, so it carries more gates than anything else.

The guards#

Guard What it prevents
Read-only means read-only A write hidden behind a read. Every line of a read-only device command is validated, not just the first, so a pasted read followed by a write cannot slip past a legitimate opening line. Only the read verbs get, show and diagnose (diag) are accepted, and a diagnose command containing a state-changing word (kill, clear, reset, delete, failover, sysrq/crash, set…, abbreviations included) is refused.
Dry run, then apply Sending a change nobody saw. Writes are computed as a minimal diff and shown before anything is sent, and every write leaves a full audit entry.
Lease locks Two operators overwriting each other. One operator holds a lease per object, refreshed by a heartbeat and re-entrant for the same user. It expires on its own (by default after 120 seconds without a heartbeat) if a browser tab is abandoned, so a closed laptop never blocks an object permanently.
Change requests gate the dangerous actions Flashing firmware outside an approved window. A live firmware upgrade refuses to run unless a change request naming the appliance is approved and the clock is inside its maintenance window. The check is repeated when the action fires, not only when it was scheduled. Every transition stamps a timeline event.

🧪Example — A refused live upgrade

A live upgrade with no approved change request in an open window is refused with: Live upgrade refused — change control: … followed by the reason (for example before the maintenance window) and the advice to run the upgrade preparation, raise a change request from it, get it approved and flash inside its window. The refusal is written to the audit log. A dry run is not gated — it sends nothing to the device.

⚠️Warning — Known limit — configuration restore

Per-device configuration restore is listed here as a limit, not as a feature. It defaults to a dry run and a live restore needs an administrator, a typed confirmation and a pre-restore backup, but there is no automated live canary round trip proving a restore end to end yet. See Configuration restore.

Where to read more#

  • Edit locks — how leases look in the editors and how to take one over.
  • Change requests and Change control — approvals and maintenance windows.
  • Firmware upgrade and Upgrade flow — the upgrade path these gates protect.
  • Device Console and SSH Console — where read-only command validation applies.
